text:
Lina (sales): CoralHealth POC follow-up. They need a concrete commit recommendation: steady state + how to handle 2x daily spikes. Workload = clinical summarization (60%) + semantic search/embeds (40%). Want HIPAA-ready Dedicated or Private. SLO target: 95th latency < 400ms for summaries.
Diego (infra): Do we have their traffic numbers?
Lina (sales): Yup: avg baseline ~60 req/s, spikes to 180 req/s for ~2 hours midday. Summaries average ~300 tokens output, embeddings request average ~512 tokens input. Prefers a 13B quantized model family; open to a smaller 7B for fallbacks.
Priya (ml): Quick calc: summaries: 180 * 0.6 * 300 ≈ 32k gen tokens/s during spike. Baseline (60 rps): ~11k tokens/s. Our runtime throughput for quantized 13B ~5k tokens/s per GPU (conservative). So baseline ~3 GPUs (11k/5k=2.2 -> 3) but spike headroom needs ~7 GPUs (32k/5k≈6.4 -> 7).
Priya (ml): Embeddings are different: embeddings throughput on a standard GPU is ~600-1200 embed ops/s depending on model. For 40% of 180 rps that's 72 embed qps at peak -> small. Could co-locate with gen pool but better to isolate if they want predictable latency. Recommend 1 dedicated embedding GPU or CPU workers if latency not strict.
Diego (infra): Recommended config: Dedicated baseline reserve = 3 gen GPUs + 1 embed GPU. Burst plan: reserved-burst credits to add +2 GPUs (up to 5) automatically, then ephemeral burst up to +2 more (spot/backfill) to reach 7 for extreme windows. Autoscale policy: step +1 GPU when 95th latency >350ms for 30s OR queue depth > baseline*0.25; cool down 8m. Preheat KV/cache 20m before expected spike.
Jon (pricing): Pricing notes: For Dedicated HIPAA, put baseline commit on term (monthly) for 3 GPUs; offer a burst-credit package sold as time-limited GPU-hours for the extra 4 GPUs. We can provide two quote options: 3 baseline + burst-pack OR 5 baseline with smaller burst. I'll prepare numbers.
Tess (security): For HIPAA/BAA we need: Private deployment with VPC peering, customer KMS, audit logs 1y, BAA signed. Also confirm PHI handling in embeddings pipeline - need assurance embeddings aren't stored cross-tenant. Lina, please get their legal contact.
Lina (sales): Getting legal contact now. They also asked: can we guarantee 95th <400ms during spikes if they commit to 3 baseline + burst credits?
Priya (ml): With 3 baseline + automatic +2 reserved burst we can meet 95th <400ms for moderate spikes (up to ~2.5x). Their 3x peak likely needs ephemeral capacity (spot/backfill) or model fallback to 7B. Recommend adding model-fallback policy: if scale cannot reach required capacity within 60s, route to 7B quantized with quality degradation notice.
Diego (infra): Ops-runbook snippet we'll hand to them: how to configure preheat window, KV warmup, cache TTLs, autoscale thresholds, and fallback routing. Also include metrics to monitor: queue_depth, tokens_per_sec, 95th_latency, provisioned_gpus.
Lina (sales): Could we give CoralHealth a quick load script to validate? They prefer something containerized.
Priya (ml): Provide this simple docker test runner:

```
# quick load test (container)
docker run --rm coralbench:latest \ 
  --target https://poc.redwood.example/v1/chat \ 
  --rps 180 --mix summaries:0.6,embeds:0.4 --avg-tokens 300 --duration 900
```

Switch rps to 60/180 to validate baseline/spike. We'll include sample prompts.
Jon (pricing): I'll attach two quote PDFs after baseline numbers are finalized. Also flag procurement cadence for Dedicated hardware order lead-time ~2-3 weeks.
Tess (security): I'll draft answers for their questionnaire: KMS integration steps, BAA text, logging retention, and embed isolation. Need contact for SOC2 report exchange.
ops-bot: Playbook created: https://redwood.internal/checklists/coralhealth-poc-capacity (items: baseline-reserve, embed-pool, burst-pack, autoscale-config, security-answers) :white_check_mark:
Lina (sales): Thanks team. Action items: Priya finalize GPU counts + fallback behavior, Diego drop ops config snippet, Jon quote options, Tess security answers. I'll schedule a 30m tech handoff with CoralHealth tomorrow afternoon.
